summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against all four paragraphs of the selected Greek. Both preserve the repentance–understanding argument, comprehensive negations, cessation of evil, lavish good, self-humbling and chastising or tormenting, and the conditions for living. The bracketed supplement is distinguished from preserved text, and the working conjecture in II.3 is retained with its reported alternative disclosed. The witness notes are consistent with the supplied bounded project reports, including distinctions between corrections, editorial emendations, damaged text and supplied fragments. Contextual repentance terminology follows current policy; no servant term occurs here. Acceptance concerns fidelity to this working source and disclosure of the supplied reports, not authentication of unseen manuscripts, independent verification of editions or exhaustive collation.
